question.text: Why is the TRUST structure the most common choice for domestic AIFs in India? Pick the best reason.

answer.text: Trusts are the only legal form permitted by SEBI for AIFs
Trusts have the shortest mandatory life (1 year) compared to LLPs (5 years) and Companies (10 years)
Trusts are exempt from SEBI registration requirements
Trusts offer operational flexibility, bespoke governance terms between Manager and beneficiaries, lower compliance cost and favourable tax treatment

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 8.4 closing paragraph: trusts dominate because of operational advantages, bespoke governance flexibility, low compliance cost, and favourable tax treatment under the determinate-trust regime. The Trap: Option A is false — LLPs, Companies and Body Corporates are all permitted. Option C is false — trusts must still register under SEBI (AIF) Regulations. Option D fabricates mandatory-life numbers. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B state the preference without explaining the governance-flexibility rationale. XIX-C requires the Manager-level reasoning. Manager's Pro-Tip: Even with the trust's governance flexibility, anchor investors often demand LP Advisory Committee (LPAC) veto rights on key-man events — bake these into the indenture rather than the IMA to give them trust-level enforceability.
